A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 20 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, objective comparisons, noise analyses and human preference studies, including Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and human studies and adds DPG-Bench results, guidance-baseline comparisons and additional quality measurements.

M1.justification: The specified procedure changes materially: v1 Eq. 3 uses quality/diversity hinge penalties, whereas v2 Eq. 2 uses directly weighted rewards with separate threshold controls. Pink-noise filtering changes from (1+f)^(-alpha) with mean/variance normalization to f^(-alpha/2) with variance-only normalization. These are substantive revisions to the reported objective and initialization; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun. Sequential generation and Flux quality reversion already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds DPG-Bench evaluation on 1,065 long, detailed prompts averaging 67 words, substantially extending testing to highly specified descriptions. GenEval and T2I-CompBench remain, including their supplementary results. COCO validation images are additionally used as an FID reference, not as a new generation task.

E2.justification: v2 supplementary Table 8 directly evaluates Particle Guidance, CADS and NegToMe against the proposed method on GenEval with Flux.1 [schnell]. v1 cited these approaches but evaluated only i.i.d. sampling and Parmar et al. as external comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds PickScore and CLIP-feature FID evaluation. Its main SDXL-Turbo DPP comparison uses HPSv2 optimization, a 150-iteration budget and revised weights/learning rate, whereas v1 Table 5 used the DPP-plus-CLIP configuration from its objective study. That original configuration remains in v2's supplement. New Flux pink-noise experiments also introduce a delayed HPSv2 reward and relative reversion threshold. Original benchmark splits and human-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing diversity-objective analysis with independent PickScore and FID checks in supplementary Table 7, and adds an explicit total-runtime comparison in Section 4.2. The original objective comparisons, noise-exponent sweep, spatial-noise analyses, human studies and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across test samples, shaded variability in the noise-change analysis, and timing errors over three seeds with measurements averaged across 100 iterations. Additional metric rows follow existing reporting practices; no new confidence intervals, significance tests or increased run counts are documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds DPG-Bench, guidance-baseline, pink-noise DPP and independent-quality results. The main SDXL-Turbo DPP comparison reports HPSv2 0.292 instead of v1's 0.261 under revised optimization settings, so this is not a fixed-setting gain; the original result remains in the supplementary objective study. The frequency-change curves also differ between v1 Fig. 6 and v2 Fig. 9. Original multi-model benchmark tables and human preference percentages are retained.

T1.justification: There are localized mathematical revisions to the loss definition and pink-noise amplitude-to-power relationship, explicitly connecting f^(-alpha/2) amplitudes to a 1/f^alpha power spectrum. The Gaussian-radius regularizer, DPP/Vendi definitions and frequency-decomposition equations remain. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: noise optimization for diversity, flexible diversity objectives, and improved diversity through low-frequency/pink-noise initialization. Rewritten contribution summaries and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains FID's limitations from mismatched COCO references and small generated samples, explicitly identifies the evaluated samplers as ODE-based, and discusses Flux's greater hyperparameter sensitivity. It also distinguishes Gaussian noise statistics from spectral whiteness. Existing objective-specific failure explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and access link, PickScore and clean-fid implementation information, and settings for new experiments, including the Flux pink-noise reward schedule. Most original GPU, resolution, regularization and objective-study hyperparameters are retained; consolidating previously stated settings into tables is primarily presentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds an explicit comparison with SliderSpace's LoRA-based diversity control and citations supporting DPG-Bench, COCO and FID evaluation. Several background diffusion references disappear with the shortened preliminaries. The central positioning against search, guidance and prompt-modification approaches remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: sequential generation moves into the method section, preliminaries are condensed, and the main experiments emphasize SDXL-Turbo/Flux and DPP. Original multi-model benchmark tables and objective-study results move into a separately titled, reorganized supplement. Contributions and explanatory passages are also rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the pipeline diagram, converts the objective-preference table into a bar chart with unchanged percentages, restructures main tables around white/pink comparisons, and adds hyperparameter and evaluation tables. Figures are extensively relocated, and new qualitative panels accompany revised sequential-generation examples and a redrawn frequency-change plot.

improvement.justification: Direct guidance comparisons, long-prompt evaluation and independent quality checks strengthen empirical support, while added access and settings information aids reproducibility. However, retained results are not reconciled with the revised loss/noise formulas, and Parmar's Flux scores differ between main Table 2 and supplementary Table 8 without a clear explanation. These reporting ambiguities limit the overall gain.
